reader_question: How is the House divided into committees and subcommittees?
grade_line: Documented: the Clerk of the House’s committee list of November 3, 2026
title: The House splits its work among 20 standing committees and three select committees, which divide it again among 109 subcommittees.
measure_line: Committees and subcommittees of the U.S. House, 119th Congress, joint committees included, as the Clerk’s file lists them
notes: Two standing committees, Budget and Ethics, have no subcommittees, and Appropriations has the most, 12, one for each of its yearly spending bills.
The Clerk’s file lists the select subcommittee on January 6, 2021, as a committee, and the chart follows it.
alt: An org chart of the House of Representatives. Under it sit 20 standing committees, three select committees and four joint committees shared with the Senate, each with its subcommittees, 109 in all. Appropriations has the most, 12; Budget, Ethics, two select committees and the joint committees have none.

table.caption: The House’s committees and their subcommittees, with the seats each side holds, from the Clerk’s file of November 3, 2026; the CSV file gives each subcommittee’s seats

chart_notes: Each committee’s box gives its count of subcommittees, each named on a row under it. Standing committees drop “Committee on”; the table gives each full name.
phone_note: Under two columns of 220 px, the committees run in one column down the page.

desk_phone.part: the first two committees; a phone draws all 27

groups.joint: {n} joint committees, shared with the Senate
